transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-20
Start: 09:27 PDT
Duration: 50 mins
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Aisha Banerjee (Redwood Solutions), Priya Raman (HorizonWorks CTO), Ethan Miles (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Ortega (Platform), Noah Price (SRE)

Summary (auto): quick qualification on p95 targets and streaming concurrency, discussed hosting options (hosted/dedicated/private), agreed to run perf harness and share detailed token/sec benchmarks; customer to share prompt set and infra constraints.

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um I think we have about 50 minutes today, quick intros?
[00:08] Priya Raman: yeah I'm Priya, CTO at HorizonWorks, we run a live conversational assistant inside our product, focused on low-latency streaming for agent chat, so p95 is critical.
[00:17] Marcus Chen: awesome, Marcus from Redwood, I'm the SE, I look after perf + hosting decisions, quick check — are you aiming for p95 on response start or full completion?
[00:27] Ethan Miles: mostly response start, we stream tokens back to users; goal is p95 start under 300ms for short replies (<=40 tokens) and p95 completion under 900ms for longer completion paths, but we're flexible if tradeoffs cost vs latency.
[00:41] Sofia Ortega: and to add, our concurrency at peak is around 120 live streaming sessions, average tokens/sec per session about 8-12, bursts up to 40 tokens/sec during heavy typing, we also have long-form summarization jobs but those are batchy.
[00:58] Lena Ortiz: great, that gives context — common choice customers face is hosted vs dedicated vs private. quick framing: hosted is easiest to start and we have conservative latency SLOs, dedicated gives reserved GPU pool and consistent throughput, private (VPC or on-prem) gives you network control and compliance; each has different routing and caching behaviors.
[01:21] Noah Price: one thing — we have strict data residency and KMS controls, must be SOC2 and enterprise KMS integration if private. how mature is Redwood's KMS path?
[01:30] Marcus Chen: we integrate with common KMS providers, HSM options for Private, and we have an SOC2 report — I'll send the artifacts, sorry I said "Redwood Dedicate" — transcription funny there — but yes, full KMS & audit log support in private mode.
[01:44] Priya Raman: perfect. also curious around KV cache and prefix caching — we reuse context a lot with system prompts and user history, does caching reduce p95 significantly for streaming?
[01:53] Marcus Chen: yes, prefix/KV cache helps a lot, especially with repeated system prompts; for streaming there's an optimization to avoid re-computing prefix tokens and to reuse KV across requests, that can shave 40-60ms p95 on short replies depending on model and seqlen. note: caching effectiveness depends on hit rate, if you have unique dynamic prompts it drops.
[02:14] Ethan Miles: what's the baseline model you're thinking? we test on a custom fine-tuned 13B (open variant) and sometimes 70B for high-quality answers — curious how Redwood handles quantized variants.
[02:25] Marcus Chen: we typically benchmark on a couple profiles: 13B fp16, 13B 4-bit quant, and a 70B int8-ish profile where supported. quantized models reduce memory and can increase throughput but may add marginal latency per token if kernel paths are different; we'll include all in the harness.
[02:40] Aisha Banerjee: also to call out, our runtime supports continuous batching and kernel selection, so for dedicated pools we can tune batch windows to hit your throughput targets without compromising streaming start times.
[02:53] [00:03:10] Speaker 1: sorry, quick clarification from Priya — when you say bursts to 40 tokens/sec, is that sustained for seconds or just milliseconds?
[03:01] Priya Raman: typically 2-5 seconds per user during rapid back-and-forth. aggregate burst across users can be heavy.
[03:08] Marcus Chen: good note, that affects autoscale and warmup strategies. two architecture patterns: 1) steady-state reserved GPUs sized for average load + burst pool, or 2) fully reserved dedicated capacity sized to peak — cost tradeoff.
[03:24] Lena Ortiz: could you share peak qps numbers? that helps us estimate required GPU vCPU mix.
[03:29] Sofia Ortega: peak qps about 150 concurrent streaming sessions, average 8 tokens/sec, peak aggregate tokens/sec ~6k for short bursts.
[03:38] Ethan Miles: and we care about p95 start for short path more than full completion latency, since UX shows users abandon if start is slow.
[03:45] Marcus Chen: understood. for that we often advise pinned model instances in Dedicated so KV and caches stay hot; Hosted can do warm pools but there is more routing variability. Private on-prem gives you most predictable network but ops overhead.
[03:58] [00:04:00] Lena Ortiz: quick qualification on timeline and decision criteria — what's your target go-live and success metrics?
[04:06] Priya Raman: we're targeting an internal pilot end of Q2, production by Q4. success metrics: p95 start < 300ms for short replies, sustained 99.5% availability during business hours, and cost per 1M tokens below $X (we'll share exact target).
[04:21] Marcus Chen: sounds reasonable. we'll map cost/lambda tradeoffs in the pricing matrix. any hard constraints on routing or region?
[04:28] Noah Price: must be in our AWS account or VPC peered; no public egress for private data. hosted is ok for non-sensitive traffic, but we want the option to shift to private for PII flows.
[04:39] Marcus Chen: VPC peering for Private is supported, we can do private control plane + customer-managed data plane, will include network diagrams in the follow-up.
[04:48] [00:04:52] Speaker 2: another question — do you have latency budgets for model cold starts?
[04:56] Ethan Miles: cold starts are painful, aim for <2s cold start but prefer to avoid via warm pools.
[05:02] Marcus Chen: we have warm pool options and reserved capacity; also keep-alive / steady heartbeats to prevent instance eviction. for streaming p95, we focus on response start pipelines and minimize RPCs.
[05:12] Priya Raman: bench numbers — can you give an example tokens/sec and p95 numbers from similar customers? even ballpark?
[05:19] Marcus Chen: sure, ballpark on a 13B quant profile on dedicated GPUs — we see ~18-25 tokens/sec per GPU for streaming workloads with small batch windows and pinned KV cache; p95 start for <=40 token replies around 150-350ms depending on network. for hosted there is slightly higher variance, maybe +50-150ms. for 70B on high-end infra, tokens/sec drops to 5-8 but quality improves.
[05:47] Lena Ortiz: note these are estimates; we'll run the harness with your prompt set to get precise numbers.
[05:53] [00:06:00] Priya Raman: what's the shape of the perf harness? what do you need from us?
[06:00] Marcus Chen: we run a replay harness that mimics streaming clients with your seqlen distribution and inter-arrival times, measure response-start p95, token/sec throughput, GPU utilization and KV hit rates. we need: sample prompt set, distribution of input lengths, and a small staging API key or endpoint to run against (we can also run in our sandbox if you prefer).
[06:19] Sofia Ortega: we want the run to include a scenario with 120 concurrent streaming clients for 30 minutes and a burst to 250 concurrent for 2-5 minutes; can you emulate that?
[06:27] Marcus Chen: yes, that's exactly what the harness can do. we'll parameterize and share the scenario config.
[06:33] [00:06:40] Speaker: slight stutter — do you support function calling / tooling while streaming?
[06:38] Aisha Banerjee: yes, Redwood supports structured outputs and tool-call patterns; streaming + tools is trickier because you need deterministic partial outputs but we have patterns to stream until tool triggers and then call out-of-band results. we'll note test cases.
[06:53] Ethan Miles: on the security side — can you restrict logs and tokens retention? also need audit log retention 12 months.
[07:01] Marcus Chen: we can configure retention and redaction, Private gives you full control, Dedicated gives configurable retention and audit logs — we'll include retention options in the security pack.
[07:10] [00:07:20] Lena Ortiz: okay, maybe quick pricing sketch — Hosted is pay-as-you-go per token, Dedicated is committed monthly capacity with discounted unit cost, Private is license + infra. we'll send a matrix.
[07:23] Priya Raman: do you have guarantees on p95 for Dedicated? any SLA language?
[07:29] Marcus Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets we can discuss in contracting; we'll surface p95 targets in the service level attachment. Hosted has standard SLOs but less strict latency guarantees.
[07:40] Lena Ortiz: to wrap, let's confirm the deliverables and owners — Marcus will run the harness and share results, I'll send pricing and SOC2/KMS docs, Priya will share prompt set and seqlen distribution, Noah will confirm network constraints.
[07:52] Priya Raman: yes that works. also can you include a quick A/B of quantized 13B vs fp16 for our prompt set? we want to see quality delta vs latency.
[08:01] Marcus Chen: absolutely — we'll include model delta bench and a short qualitative eval.
[08:07] [00:08:10] Speaker 3: one more — do you support canary/fallback policies across models to keep service up if a model fails or overloaded?
[08:14] Aisha Banerjee: yes, Redwood routing supports model variants and automatic fallback to cheaper variants or lower-precision quantized models; you can set policy by latency or cost thresholds.
[08:26] Ethan Miles: that could be useful — we might want canary traffic to a cheaper quantized variant during heavy periods.
[08:31] Marcus Chen: we can demo that in the follow-up.
[08:34] Lena Ortiz: awesome. i'll propose 2026-03-30 for the follow-up deep-dive after we share the harness results, does that work?
[08:41] Priya Raman: yes, 03-30 works for us.
[08:45] [00:09:00] Lena Ortiz: cool, thanks all. I'll recap in an email.
[08:49] Priya Raman: thanks everyone.
[08:51] Ethan Miles: thanks.
[08:52] Sofia Ortega: bye.
[08:53] Noah Price: bye.

Recap / Notes:
- Customer wants p95 start < 300ms short replies, 120-250 concurrent streaming sessions in different scenarios, sample prompt distribution to be provided.
- Redwood to run perf harness across 13B fp16, 13B quant, and 70B profiles; include A/B quality delta.
- Security docs: SOC2, KMS integration, audit log retention options.
- Next meeting proposed: 2026-03-30 to review benchmarks.

References mentioned: perf harness config (will be shared), token/sec spreadsheet (link placeholder), SOC2 report (to be attached).

Transcript end.
